claim_text: Poisoned sheep/meat was presented to Muhammad in the Khaybar context
Muhammad ate/tasted from the poisoned sheep
The poisoning was deliberate and intended to kill or eliminate Muhammad
The perpetrator is described in multiple early reports as a Jewish woman
The woman was Zaynab bint al-Harith
Bishr ibn al-Bara died after eating from the poisoned sheep
Muhammad initially declined the companions' proposal to kill the woman
The woman was later executed after Bishr's death
During his final illness Muhammad reportedly connected continuing pain to the food eaten at Khaybar
The Khaybar poison was the direct medical cause of Muhammad's death years later
Poison was concentrated in the foreleg because it was reported to be Muhammad's preferred part
The poisoning was motivated specifically by revenge for named relatives killed at Khaybar
Quraysh plotted against Muhammad and killing him was one explicit option
The plot also included restraint/detention and expulsion as alternatives
The plot belonged to the Meccan period immediately before Muhammad's departure
A decisive council concerning Muhammad met at Dar al-Nadwah
Abu Jahl proposed a joint multi-clan plan to kill Muhammad
The multi-clan rationale was to distribute blood liability so one clan could not be singled out
An elder from Najd identified in the tradition with Iblis participated in the council
Muhammad was warned not to sleep in his usual place and was permitted to depart
Ali slept in Muhammad's usual sleeping place on the night of departure
Hostile watchers remained at Muhammad's sleeping place expecting to seize or kill him
Muhammad escaped the hostile search and Quraysh pursued him toward the cave
A spider web at the cave caused pursuers to turn away
The exact speeches preserved for participants at Dar al-Nadwah reproduce their historical wording
